claims.statement: In the specified 1,836-encoding labeled Prüfer sample of orders 8 through 16, there are 37 eligible parameter rows; all have p=x+2, select every original leaf, have S<0, and satisfy E<=(x+1)Q. No sampled eligible row has a proper favorable-leaf selector.
claims.scope: Only the seeded, shape-biased labeled Prüfer sample and exact arithmetic protocol in REPORT.md and EVIDENCE.json. This is bounded evidence and makes no universal claim about ordinary trees.
claims.reason: The complete eligible-row ledger records graph edges, original leaves, every leaf's Delta_p(T-v), selector membership, selected supports and summands, and exact aggregate counts; the replay script asserts the stated identities. The run found zero proper-selector examples and zero positive aggregates, so it neither proves nor refutes the universal target.

limitations: The Prüfer protocol samples labeled trees and retains isomorphic duplicates; it is not exhaustive at any searched order.
No proper favorable-leaf selector occurred in the eligible sample, so the route did not achieve the primary proper-selector stress objective.
All eligible rows had p=x+2, so this sample does not separate the CT_x and current-rank addability budgets.
Finite negative aggregates and positive budget gaps do not prove the universal aggregate or CT_x bound.
